jobs.title: Sun 022 first cut v01
jobs.body:
Sun 022 first cut v01, up by Fri 9 Oct 18:00 London (review Sat 10, final OK Tue 13).
Spec: 02_Video-Projects/022_Is-the-Sun-Getting-Brighter/07_Edit-Project/shot_list_v01.csv (104 shots on the locked VO, 502.64 s) and SHOT_LIST_v01.md (rules). Full brief: #99 6036709461.
- NASA stills from nasa_pool_v01.json `orig` URLs: 16:9 fill + feathered blur, upscale <= ~2.35x, Ken Burns as listed, crop SDO corner timestamps.
- SVS motion muted, clean stretches, max 2 per clip. Code graphics: code_graphics.py zoom_nolabels / core_nolabels / clocks.
- `grade` column: young Sun -30% and cooler, future Sun +10% and scale 1.04. No red giant.
- OMNI rows: Vertex free credit only, one take each; if Omni fails use the row's `fallback`. Never let Omni hold up the cut.
- Lower-third chapter cards ~2.5 s; -14 LUFS; music full runtime; end on SVS 10925 held 16 s.
- Listen at 457.04 s: words.json hears "Free clocks" (script: "Three clocks"). Say what you hear.
Done = mp4 path, frame sheets, clip_check output, which OMNI rows used fallback, posted on #99.

jobs.title: Decide: install the Cursor worker
jobs.body: Decide whether to install the Cursor worker (scripts/mini/com.owb.cursor-worker.plist): it lets Cursor run commands on the Mini unattended every 30 min, under the written rules, so jobs move while Grok Bot is out. Install commands are in the plist header.

history.what: cancelled: Ben decided 7 Oct: yes, and wider. Replaced by the Chief relay (5b60eff): Grok, then Cursor, then Codex act as Chief, whoever is up. Install is J0006.

jobs.title: Install the Chief relay on the Mini
jobs.body:
Install the Chief relay on the Mini (Ben asked for it, 7 Oct; AGENTS.md "Chief relay"). Free; nothing on YouTube.

    cd ~/YouTube/orbit-with-ben && git pull
    mkdir -p ~/_desk/bin ~/_desk/state && cp scripts/chief_relay.py ~/_desk/bin/
    cp scripts/mini/com.owb.chief-relay.plist ~/Library/LaunchAgents/
    launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.owb.chief-relay.plist
    python3 ~/_desk/bin/chief_relay.py status

Then check, and put each result in the done note:
- `status` shows Cursor UP and, if Codex is installed, Codex UP. Grok shows down until it runs jobs.py.
- `codex exec --help` lists `--full-auto`, `--add-dir` and `-c`. If a flag is missing, set CODEX_FLAGS in the plist
  (an EnvironmentVariables dict) to what this version accepts, and say what you set.
- If a ~/_desk/state/cursor-covers-chief file exists from the old worker, delete it. It does nothing now.
- After the first run, the end of ~/Library/Logs/chief-relay.log.
jobs.result: Relay installed and running (launchd com.owb.chief-relay, pid 59393, first run 13:08 woke Cursor); ~/_desk/bin script and LaunchAgents plist match the repo. status: Grok down (no heartbeat), Cursor UP, Codex UP. Codex 0.160.0 has no --full-auto: installed plist now sets CODEX_FLAGS='exec -s workspace-write --approve-for-me -c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true --add-dir "<HOS>" --add-dir ~/_desk'. Also set CODEX_BIN=~/.npm-global/bin/codex (launchd's zsh -lc PATH missed it: log said codex 'CLI not installed') and HOS_REPO='~/YouTube/History Of Science' (default history-of-science doesn't exist). Same three via launchctl setenv so they apply without a reload. Old cursor-covers-chief deleted. Log tail: chain chief=down | cursor=UP | codex=down (CLI not installed) [pre-fix]; run: cursor (cap 1500s).

jobs.title: Gemini: Sun 022 pictures vs words, and the clock numbers
jobs.body:
Gemini (agy) check of the Sun 022 pictures and graphic numbers, before the first cut's review pack (Fri 9 Oct).
No spend. Don't edit the shot list or the script; report only.

1. Picture vs words. For every GODDARD and NASA row in 02_Video-Projects/022_Is-the-Sun-Getting-Brighter/07_Edit-Project/shot_list_v01.csv:
   open the source page (svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/<id> for SVS ids; images.nasa.gov or the NASA page for the rest) and record
   what it really shows: instrument, wavelength, date, and whether it is a real observation or a visualisation.
   Flag any row where the VO line at that moment says something the picture isn't, for example "flare" over a
   prominence, today's Sun under a line about the young Sun, or a simulation shown as if it were film.
2. Numbers in the code graphics. clocks.mp4 (row 96) draws three clocks: about 1% per 110 million years; about 0.1% up
   and down over the 11-year cycle; a prominence lasting about a day. Check each one against 01_Script/SOURCES.md and
   the primary source, with the exact quote.
3. Write 07_Edit-Project/GEMINI_PICTURE_CHECK_v01.md: one table row per flagged shot (row, id, what it shows, the VO
   line, why it's wrong, a suggested swap from the row's fallback or NASA_POOL_v01.md), then the clock numbers, then
   "all other rows OK" with the count. Commit it and mark the job done with the commit.
Claude decides every swap.

jobs.title: Chief relay checks on the Mini
jobs.body:
Chief relay checks on the Mini (Claude, #99 6037855513 and 6038325583). Quick, free, read-only apart from step 2.
1. cp scripts/chief_relay.py ~/_desk/bin/  then  python3 ~/_desk/bin/chief_relay.py status  (paste the output)
2. rm ~/_desk/state/chief/current.json   (so the next relay run posts its handover line again)
3. ls -lt "$HOME/Library/Application Support/Grok Bot/dune-reliability/sessions" | head
   Does it exist, and when was the newest file written? If this Grok Bot version keeps sessions elsewhere, find the
   folder it writes to while it works and give the path (it goes in GROK_SESSIONS_DIR).
4. After the next relay run: grep "notify failed" ~/Library/Logs/chief-relay.log  and report the line, if any.
   Never put a token in the plist; say what you find.
